title: SharePoint: Copilot Site Builder creates a site after users confirm a plan
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing, credit requirement and both control routes are supported. It correctly reports the conflicting preview and general-availability guidance rather than assuming a Site Builder default. Another Microsoft page uses a different label for Restricted Content Discovery, which should be noted.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes Copilot and AI entry points from the sites it covers.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery also removes AI-powered entry points from these SharePoint sites. Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery affects discoverability rather than access permissions.
claims.quote: No. Restricted Content Discovery affects discoverability, not access permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access it.

claims.claim: The control is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path. Add to the control note: 'Microsoft's readiness guide instead labels this setting Restrict content discovery > On.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/get-ready-copilot-sharepoint-advanced-management#step-3-prevent-accidental-oversharing, which says 'Under Restrict content discovery, select On.'

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Delegating Restricted Content Discovery management to site administrators requires a separate tenant setting.
claims.quote: If you want site administrators to manage the setting for their own sites, enable delegation by using the following PowerShell command: Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement $true
